author: Peter X. K. Song
text: We introduce a novel statistical procedure for clustering categorical data based on Hamming distance HD vectors The proposed method is conceptually simple and computationally straightforward because it does not require any specific statistical models or any convergence criteria Moreover unlike most currently existing algorithms that compute the class membership or membership probability for every data point at each iteration our algorithm sequentially extracts clusters from the given dataset That is at each iteration our algorithm strives to identify only one cluster which will then be deleted from the dataset at the next iteration this procedure repeats until there are no more significant clusters in the remaining data Consequently the number of clusters can be determined automatically by the algorithm As for the identification and extraction of a cluster we first locate the cluster center by using a Pearson chisquaredtype statistic on the basis of HD vectors The partition of the dataset produced by our algorithm is unique and insensitive to the input order of data points The performance of the proposed algorithm is examined using both simulated and real world datasets Comparisons with two wellknown clustering algorithms Kmodes and AutoClass show that the proposed algorithm substantially outperforms these competitors with the classification rate or the information gain typically improved by several orders of magnitude Computational complexity and run time comparisons are also provided

author: Peter X. K. Song
text: This paper addresses the challenge of efficient estimation in additive hazards regression models when applied to current status data Current status data where the exact time of an event is unobserved is common in various fields such as epidemiology and social sciences We propose a novel estimation method that incorporates a flexible approach to the nonparametric component of the additive hazards model enhancing the robustness of parameter estimates under current status constraints The methodology leverages an innovative penalized likelihood framework allowing for the simultaneous estimation of both fixed and random effects in the presence of censored data We establish the asymptotic properties of our estimators demonstrating consistency and asymptotic normality Through extensive simulation studies we evaluate the performance of our proposed method in comparison to existing techniques particularly focusing on bias variance and predictive accuracy Our results indicate significant improvements in estimation efficiency particularly in scenarios with high levels of censoring Finally we apply our methodology to a realworld dataset illustrating its practical implications and potential for advancing the analysis of survival data under current status conditions This work contributes to the understanding of additive hazards models and offers a robust tool for researchers dealing with incomplete survival information

author: Peter X. K. Song
text: This paper concerns the analysis of discretevalued time series using a class of categorical ARMA models recently proposed by Biswas and Song Such ARMA processes are flexible to model discretevalued time series allowing a wide range of marginal distributions such as binomial multinomial Poisson and nominalordinal categorical probability mass functions To apply these models in the data analysis this paper focuses on the development of a needed statistical toolbox which includes maximum likelihood estimation and inference model selection and goodnessoffit test Particularly in AR models a biascorrected AIC statistic is derived for the order selection while a randomized conditional moment RCM test is furnished to examine the goodnessoffit Finitesample performances of the proposed methods are examined through simulation studies in which the biascorrected AIC is shown to outperform the traditional AIC and BIC statistics and the RCM test achieves desirable power As part of the numeric illustration a data analysis of categorical time series on infant sleep quality is provided by the application of this new toolbox C Elsevier BV

author: Peter X. K. Song
text: It has been a long history of using interactions in regression analysis to investigate alterations in covariateeffects on response variables In this article we aim to address two kinds of new challenges arising from the inclusion of such highorder effects in the regression model for complex data The first kind concerns a situation where interaction effects of individual covariates are weak but those of combined covariates are strong and the other kind pertains to the presence of nonlinear interactive effects directed by loweffect covariates We propose a new class of semiparametric models with varying index coefficients which enables us to model and assess nonlinear interaction effects between grouped covariates on the response variable As a result most of the existing semiparametric regression models are special cases of our proposed models We develop a numerically stable and computationally fast estimation procedure using both profile least squares method and local fitting We establish both estimation consistency and asymptotic normality for the proposed estimators of index coefficients as well as the oracle property for the nonparametric function estimator In addition a generalized likelihood ratio test is provided to test for the existence of interaction effects or the existence of nonlinear interaction effects Our models and estimation methods are illustrated by simulation studies and by an analysis of child growth data to evaluate alterations in growth rates incurred by mothers exposures to endocrine disrupting compounds during pregnancy Supplementary materials for this article are available online

author: Peter X. K. Song
text: The method of composite likelihood is useful for dealing with estimation and inference in parametric models with highdimensional data where the full likelihood approach renders computation intractable We develop an extension of the EM algorithm in the framework of composite likelihood estimation given missing data or latent variables We establish key theoretical properties of the composite likelihood EM CLEM algorithm the ascent property algorithmic convergence and convergence rate The proposed method is applied to estimate the transition probabilities in a multivariate hidden Markov model Simulation studies are presented to demonstrate the empirical performance of the method A timecourse microarray data is analyzed using the proposed CLEM method to dissect the underlying gene regulatory network

author: Peter X. K. Song
text: In this paper we propose a novel approach for estimating parameters in spatialclustered data using an efficient pairwise composite likelihood framework Spatialclustered data which often arise in fields such as ecology epidemiology and social sciences exhibit complex dependencies that traditional independent or parametric methods fail to capture adequately Our methodology leverages the pairwise composite likelihood which allows for a flexible modeling of spatial dependencies by directly utilizing pairwise relationships among observations within clusters We establish the theoretical properties of our estimator demonstrating its consistency and asymptotic normality Additionally we introduce computational algorithms that enhance the efficiency of the estimation process reducing the time complexity associated with large datasets Simulation studies and realdata applications illustrate the robustness of our approach compared to existing methods revealing improved parameter estimation accuracy and predictive capability This framework not only advances the statistical toolbox for analyzing spatialclustered data but also provides practitioners with an effective means to derive insights from complex dependencies inherent in their datasets

author: Peter X. K. Song
text: In this paper we present a novel nonparametric inference approach for detecting local extrema in highdimensional data particularly focusing on oligonucleotide microarray datasets derived from yeast genome studies Traditional parametric methods often rely on assumptions that may not hold in the context of complex biological data leading to potential biases in identifying significant maxima and minima Our proposed methodology employs kernel smoothing techniques combined with rankbased tests to robustly estimate the underlying distribution of gene expression levels and to detect local extrema without imposing strict parametric constraints We validate our approach through comprehensive simulations that demonstrate superior performance over existing methods in terms of both type I error rates and power Additionally we apply our nonparametric framework to a comprehensive yeast microarray dataset revealing biologically relevant local extrema that correlate with known gene functions and pathways Our results emphasize the effectiveness of nonparametric inference in elucidating critical patterns within genomic data thereby contributing to the broader field of statistical genomics We conclude by discussing the implications of our findings for future studies aimed at understanding the regulatory mechanisms of gene expression in yeast and beyond

author: Peter X. K. Song
text: In this paper we introduce a novel Composite Likelihood ExpectationMaximization EM algorithm tailored for the estimation of parameters in multivariate Hidden Markov Models HMMs Traditional EM algorithms often face challenges when dealing with highdimensional data or complex dependencies which can lead to difficulties in convergence and computational efficiency We address these limitations by leveraging composite likelihood approaches that enable efficient estimation by focusing on the marginal likelihoods of subsets of observations thereby reducing computational burden while maintaining statistical robustness Our proposed method is rigorously derived and its convergence properties are established We demonstrate the practicality of the Composite Likelihood EM algorithm through comprehensive simulations and realworld applications in fields such as finance and bioinformatics where multivariate dependencies are prevalent Comparative analyses reveal significant performance improvements over standard EM methods particularly in situations characterized by limited sample sizes or intricate correlation structures The results substantiate the efficacy of the Composite Likelihood EM algorithm as a powerful tool for statistical inference in multivariate HMMs paving the way for future research in complex model estimation

author: Peter X. K. Song
text: In this paper we introduce Varying Index Coefficient Models VICMs as a flexible framework for analyzing complex relationships in highdimensional data Traditional statistical models often rely on fixed coefficients which can inadequately capture the dynamic nature of certain phenomena Our proposed VICM addresses this limitation by allowing the index coefficients to vary as functions of observed covariates thus enabling deeper insights into the heterogeneous effects of predictors across different contexts We provide a comprehensive theoretical foundation for the model including estimation and inference techniques and demonstrate its advantages through simulations and realworld applications The results indicate that VICMs outperform conventional models in terms of predictive accuracy and interpretability particularly in scenarios where interactions among variables are prevalent This work contributes to the growing field of flexible modeling approaches and offers valuable methodological tools for researchers dealing with complex datasets where conventional assumptions may not hold

author: Peter X. K. Song
text: In longitudinal studies continuous proportional data often arise in diverse fields such as biology medicine and social sciences However the inherent bounded nature of such data can violate standard assumptions of linear models leading to biased estimates and invalid inferences This paper introduces a novel framework of Robust Transformation Mixedeffects Models RTMM specifically designed to address these challenges Our approach incorporates a robust transformation technique that effectively mitigates the impact of outliers and nonnormality in proportional data By combining this transformation with mixedeffects modeling we accommodate both fixed and random effects facilitating the analysis of repeated measures across individuals We evaluate the performance of RTMM through extensive simulation studies demonstrating its superior robustness and flexibility compared to traditional methods Additionally we apply our proposed model to a realworld dataset showcasing its practical utility in deriving meaningful insights while ensuring valid statistical inference The findings indicate that RTMM not only improves accuracy in parameter estimation but also enhances the reliability of predictions making it a valuable contribution to the statistical analysis of longitudinal proportion data

author: Peter X. K. Song
text: In longitudinal data analysis with dropouts despite its local efficiency in theory the augmented inverse probability weighted AIPW estimator hardly achieves the semiparametric efficiency bound in practice even if the variancecovariance of the longitudinal outcomes is correctly modeled In this paper we propose a method based on conditional empirical likelihood Assuming missing at random MAR mechanism our estimator is doubly robust and locally efficient Unlike the AIPW estimator our estimator does not require to model any second moments including the variancecovariance of the longitudinal outcomes in order to achieve the semiparametric efficiency bound C Elsevier Inc

author: Peter X. K. Song
text: In longitudinal data analysis the presence of dropouts poses significant challenges to the estimation of population parameters often leading to inefficiencies and biased results This paper addresses these issues by exploring the conditions under which semiparametric efficiency bounds can be achieved in the presence of missing data due to dropout mechanisms We propose a comprehensive framework that builds on the principles of targeted maximum likelihood estimation TMLE and use of dynamic models to account for the dropout process explicitly Through a series of simulation studies we demonstrate the improved efficiency and robustness of our proposed methodology compared to traditional approaches which frequently rely on parametric assumptions or complete case analyses Additionally we apply our method to a realworld dataset on patient responses in a clinical trial illustrating its practical utility and the valuable insights it can provide in overcoming dropoutrelated biases Our findings establish a clear pathway for achieving semiparametric efficiency in longitudinal studies ultimately contributing to more reliable estimates and informed decisionmaking in research settings that routinely encounter dropout issues

author: Peter X. K. Song
text: Identifying local extrema of expression profiles is one primary objective in some cDNA microarray experiments To study the replication dynamics of the yeast genome for example local peaks of hybridization intensity profiles correspond to putative replication origins We propose a nonparametric kernel smoothing NKS technique to detect local hybridization intensity extrema across chromosomes The novelty of our approach is that we base our inference procedures on equilibrium points namely those locations at which the first derivative of the intensity curve is zero The proposed smoothing technique provides both point and interval estimation for the location of local extrema Also this technique can be used to test for the hypothesis of either one or multiple suspected locations being the true equilibrium points We illustrate the proposed method on a microarray data set from an experiment designed to study the replication origins in the yeast genome in that the locations of autonomous replication sequence ARS elements are identified through the equilibrium points of the smoothed intensity profile curve Our method found a few ARS elements that were not detected by the current smoothing methods such as the Fourier convolution smoothing

author: Peter X. K. Song
text: Clustering categorical data poses unique challenges due to the nonnumeric nature of the data which often requires specialized distance metrics to accurately capture the relationships among different categories This paper presents a novel approach to clustering categorical data using distance vectors which are generated based on a modified version of the Gower distance to account for varied types of categorical attributes We define distance vectors that encapsulate the pairwise similarities across multiple categorical features and propose a clustering algorithm that leverages these vectors to effectively group similar instances Through extensive experiments on several benchmark datasets we demonstrate that our method outperforms traditional clustering techniques such as kmodes and hierarchical clustering in terms of clustering quality and interpretability Our results indicate that the incorporation of distance vectors not only improves clustering performance but also enhances the understanding of categorical data structures This paper contributes to the growing body of research on advanced clustering techniques and provides practical insights for researchers and practitioners working with categorical datasets

author: Peter X. K. Song
text: AbstractThis paper presents a comprehensive statistical analysis of discretevalued time series data utilizing categorical AutoRegressive Moving Average ARMA models As discretevalued time series are prevalent in various fields such as finance epidemiology and social sciences traditional continuousvalued modeling techniques often fall short in capturing their underlying structure We introduce a novel framework that extends the ARMA modeling approach to accommodate categorical data specifically focusing on the nonnegative integer and ordinal categories Our methodology involves the development of estimation techniques and diagnostic tools tailored for categorical ARMA models enabling the identification of significant patterns and dependencies within the data We apply our proposed approach to simulated datasets as well as realworld examples demonstrating its efficacy in forecasting and analysis Results highlight the advantages of using categorical ARMA models over classical methods revealing insights into the dynamics of discrete time series that prior models could not uncover This work contributes to the existing literature by providing a robust statistical foundation for analyzing discretevalued time series offering a valuable tool for researchers and practitioners in diverse disciplines

author: Peter X. K. Song
text: We address the matter of determining whether or not missing data in longitudinal studies are ignorable with regard to quasilikelihood or estimating equations approaches This involves testing for whether or not the zeromean property of estimating equations holds true Chen Little proposed testing for significant differences among parameter estimators calculated from sample subsets with different patterns of missing data whereas we propose a more unified generalised scoretype test This avoids exhaustive estimation of parameters for each missingdata pattern testing instead with a single quadratic score test statistic whether or not there is a common parameter under which the means of all the patternspecific estimating equations are zero Comparisons are made for the two approaches with both simulations and real data examples

author: Peter X. K. Song
text: This paper studies a new approach to longitudinal data analysis using the conditional empirical likelihood CEL method within the framework of marginal models The possible unbalanced followup visits are dealt with via stratification according to distinctive followup patterns The CEL method does not require any explicit modelling of the variancecovariance of the longitudinal outcomes Instead it implicitly incorporates a consistently estimated variancecovariance matrix in a nonparametric fashion The proposed CEL estimator is connected to the generalized estimating equations GEE estimator and achieves the same efficiency as the GEE estimator employing the true variancecovariance The asymptotic distribution of the CEL estimator is derived and simulation studies are conducted to assess the finite sample performance Data collected from a longitudinal nutrition study are analysed as an application C Statistical Society of Canada

author: Peter X. K. Song
text: This paper presents a unified framework of stationary ARMA processes for discretevalued time series based on Pegrams Pegram GGS An autoregressive model for multilag markov chains J Appl Probab mixing operator Such a stochastic operator appears to be more flexible than the currently popular thinning operator to construct Box and Jenkins type stationary ARMA processes with arbitrary discrete marginal distributions This flexibility allows us to yield an ARMA model for time series of binomial or categorical observations as a special case which was unavailable with the extended thinning operator Joe H Time series models with univariate margins in the convolutionclosed infinitely divisible class J Appl Probab because the binomialcategorical distribution is not infinitely divisible We also study parameter estimation and comparison with the thinning operator based method whenever applicable Real data examples are used to examine and illustrate the proposed method C Elsevier BV

author: Peter X. K. Song
text: This paper presents a comprehensive exploration of longitudinal data analysis leveraging the Conditional Empirical Likelihood CEL method Longitudinal datasets characterized by repeated observations over time for the same subjects pose unique statistical challenges particularly in addressing issues of correlation and missing data The CEL method known for its robustness and flexibility allows for efficient estimation of parameters while accommodating complex structures inherent in longitudinal studies We begin by outlining the theoretical foundations of the CEL approach followed by its application to various longitudinal data scenarios including balanced and unbalanced designs Through extensive simulations we demonstrate the performance of the CEL method in terms of bias efficiency and robustness compared to traditional estimation techniques such as Generalized Estimating Equations GEEs and MixedEffects Models Additionally we provide realworld case studies from health and social sciences to illustrate the practical utility of the CEL method in extracting meaningful insights from longitudinal data Our findings suggest that the Conditional Empirical Likelihood serves as a powerful tool in the statistical toolkit for analyzing longitudinal data offering an improved framework for research across diverse fields We conclude with recommendations for future research directions and the potential integration of the CEL method into existing statistical software packages

author: Peter X. K. Song
text: This article presents a new modeling strategy in functional data analysis We consider the problem of estimating an unknown smooth function given functional data with noise The unknown function is treated as the realization of a stochastic process which is incorporated into a diffusion model The method of smoothing spline estimation is connected to a special case of this approach The resulting models offer great flexibility to capture the dynamic features of functional data and allow straightforward and meaningful interpretation The likelihood of the models is derived with Euler approximation and data augmentation A unified Bayesian inference method is carried out via a Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm including a simulation smoother The proposed models and methods are illustrated on some prostatespecific antigen data where we also show how the models can be used for forecasting

author: Peter X. K. Song
text: The method of composite likelihood is useful for dealing with estimation and inference in parametric models with highdimensional data where the full likelihood approach renders computation intractable We develop an extension of the EM algorithm in the framework of composite likelihood estimation given missing data or latent variables We establish key theoretical properties of the composite likelihood EM CLEM algorithm the ascent property algorithmic convergence and convergence rate The proposed method is applied to estimate the transition probabilities in a multivariate hidden Markov model Simulation studies are presented to demonstrate the empirical performance of the method A timecourse microarray data is analyzed using the proposed CLEM method to dissect the underlying gene regulatory network

author: Peter X. K. Song
text: The integration of multiple longitudinal studies presents unique challenges particularly when faced with studyspecific missing covariates that can bias estimates and hinder the robustness of conclusions This paper introduces a novel joint estimating function approach designed to effectively merge diverse datasets while simultaneously addressing the complications posed by nonrandomly missing covariates We employ a framework that incorporates information from all available studies allowing for flexible modeling of the longitudinal data structure alongside missingness patterns Our methodology leverages the strengths of generalized estimating equations GEEs and multiple imputation techniques to derive consistent estimates of model parameters and standard errors We validate our approach through extensive simulations that demonstrate improved performance over traditional methods in terms of bias reduction and efficiency Additionally we apply our framework to a realworld dataset comprising several health studies illustrating how our method enables comprehensive analyses and enhances the generalizability of findings across different populations Our results underscore the importance of properly addressing missing covariates in longitudinal studies setting the stage for future research in this critical area

author: Peter X. K. Song
text: Merging multiple datasets collected from studies with identical or similar scientific objectives is often undertaken in practice to increase statistical power This article concerns the development of an effective statistical method that enables to merge multiple longitudinal datasets subject to various heterogeneous characteristics such as different followup schedules and studyspecific missing covariates eg covariates observed in some studies but missing in other studies The presence of studyspecific missing covariates presents great statistical methodology challenge in data merging and analysis We propose a joint estimating function approach to addressing this challenge in which a novel nonparametric estimating function constructed via splinesbased sieve approximation is utilized to bridge estimating equations from studies with missing covariates to those with fully observed covariates Under mild regularity conditions we show that the proposed estimator is consistent and asymptotically normal We evaluate finitesample performances of the proposed method through simulation studies In comparison to the conventional multiple imputation approach our method exhibits smaller estimation bias We provide an illustrative data analysis using longitudinal cohorts collected in Mexico City to assess the effect of lead exposures on childrens somatic growth

author: Peter X. K. Song
text: This paper focuses on the problem of maximum likelihood estimation in linear mixedeffects models where outliers or unduly large observations are present in clustered or longitudinal data Multivariate t distributions are often imposed on either random effects andor random errors to incorporate outliers A powerful algorithm of maximum by parts MBP proposed by Song Fan and Kalbfleisch is implemented to obtain maximum likelihood estimators when the likelihood is intractable The computational efficiency of the MBP allows us to further apply a profilelikelihood technique for the estimation of the degrees of freedom in tdistributions Comparison of the Akaike information criterion AIC among candidate models provides an objective criterion to determine whether outliers are influential on the quality of model fit The proposed models and methods are illustrated through both simulation studies and data analysis examples with comparison to the existing EMalgorithm

author: Peter X. K. Song
text: In this paper we introduce a novel Composite Likelihood ExpectationMaximization EM algorithm tailored for the estimation of parameters in multivariate Hidden Markov Models HMMs Traditional EM algorithms often face challenges when dealing with highdimensional data or complex dependencies which can lead to difficulties in convergence and computational efficiency We address these limitations by leveraging composite likelihood approaches that enable efficient estimation by focusing on the marginal likelihoods of subsets of observations thereby reducing computational burden while maintaining statistical robustness Our proposed method is rigorously derived and its convergence properties are established We demonstrate the practicality of the Composite Likelihood EM algorithm through comprehensive simulations and realworld applications in fields such as finance and bioinformatics where multivariate dependencies are prevalent Comparative analyses reveal significant performance improvements over standard EM methods particularly in situations characterized by limited sample sizes or intricate correlation structures The results substantiate the efficacy of the Composite Likelihood EM algorithm as a powerful tool for statistical inference in multivariate HMMs paving the way for future research in complex model estimation

author: Peter X. K. Song
text: In this paper we propose a novel approach for maximum likelihood inference in robust linear mixedeffects models by leveraging the flexibility of multivariate t distributions Traditional linear mixedeffects models often assume normality in the error structure which can lead to biased estimates and unreliable inference when faced with outliers or nonnormality in the data To address this limitation we introduce an augmented formulation of the linear mixedeffects model incorporating multivariate t distributions that allow for heavier tails and greater robustness against deviations from normality We derive the maximum likelihood estimates for the model parameters using a tailored ExpectationMaximization EM algorithm which facilitates convergence even in the presence of complex data structure Through simulation studies and realworld applications we demonstrate the efficacy of our proposed method in providing accurate parameter estimates improved robustness and valid inference compared to existing approaches Our findings highlight the advantages of utilizing multivariate t distributions in capturing the inherent variability of data thereby extending the applicability of mixedeffects modeling in fields such as psychology biology and social sciences where data irregularities are common

author: Peter X. K. Song
text: AbstractIn this paper we present a novel approach to Stochastic Functional Data Analysis SFDA through the lens of diffusion modeling Traditional methods for analyzing functional data often assume deterministic structures which may overlook the inherent stochasticity present in many realworld processes Our diffusion modelbased framework accommodates the continuous and random nature of functional observations allowing for a more nuanced understanding of the underlying phenomenaWe rigorously define a diffusion model that captures the dynamics of functional data over time incorporating both temporal dependence and intrinsic variability This model is evaluated through a comprehensive simulation study highlighting its robustness under various noise conditions and functional shapes We further illustrate the practical applicability of our approach through case studies in diverse fields including finance biostatistics and environmental scienceOur findings demonstrate that the proposed diffusion model not only enhances the accuracy of functional data estimation but also provides insightful statistical inferences regarding the underlying processes We conclude by discussing the implications of our work for future research in SFDA and potential extensions of the diffusion model in other statistical domains

author: Peter X. K. Song
text: Diagnostics for heteroscedasticity in linear regression models have been intensively investigated in the literature However limited attention has been paid on how to identify covariates associated with heteroscedastic error variances This problem is critical in correctly modelling the variance structure in weighted least squares estimation which leads to improved estimation efficiency We propose covariatespecific statistics based on information ratios formed as comparisons between the modelbased and sandwich variance estimators A twostep diagnostic procedure is established first to detect heteroscedasticity in error variances and then to identify covariates the error variance structure might depend on This proposed method is generalized to accommodate practical complications such as when covariates associated with the heteroscedastic variances might not be associated with the mean structure of the response variable or when strong correlation is present amongst covariates The performance of the proposed method is assessed via a simulation study and is illustrated through a data analysis in which we show the importance of correct identification of covariates associated with the variance structure in estimation and inference C Statistical Society of Canada

author: Peter X. K. Song
text: Heteroscedasticity the phenomenon where the variability of the error terms in a regression model is not constant across all levels of the independent variables poses significant challenges in statistical analysis and inference This paper presents a comprehensive examination of heteroscedasticity in linear regression models focusing on its identification implications and remediation Utilizing both graphical and statistical tests we introduce a systematic profiling approach that enhances the detection of heteroscedastic patterns across various datasets We demonstrate how traditional methods such as the BreuschPagan and White tests can be augmented with modern machine learning techniques to better characterize variability structures Moreover we explore the impact of different forms of heteroscedasticity on estimates and hypothesis testing offering tailored strategies for model adjustment including robust standard errors and generalized least squares Through simulations and realworld applications we illustrate the effectiveness of our proposed profiling methodology in improving model accuracy and reliability This work aims to provide practitioners with a robust framework for understanding and addressing heteroscedasticity in their regression analyses fostering more reliable inferential conclusions

author: Peter X. K. Song
text: AbstractIn this paper we introduce and explore discretevalued ARMA Autoregressive Moving Average processes a class of stochastic models specifically designed to analyze and forecast time series data consisting of discrete observations We develop a theoretical framework that extends traditional ARMA processes to accommodate noncontinuous data which are common in various fields such as economics biology and social sciences By employing a combination of probabilistic techniques and discrete probability distributions we derive properties of these models including stationarity invertibility and the identification of model parameters We utilize simulation studies to validate our theoretical findings and demonstrate the practical applications of discretevalued ARMA processes through illustrative examples including count data and binary response scenarios Furthermore we compare the performance of our proposed models to existing discretetime models showcasing their advantages in capturing the inherent structures of time series with discrete outcomes Our findings lay the groundwork for future research in the domain of discrete time series analysis providing a robust statistical tool for practitioners faced with discretevalued data

author: Peter X. K. Song
text: In longitudinal data analysis the presence of dropouts poses significant challenges to the estimation of population parameters often leading to inefficiencies and biased results This paper addresses these issues by exploring the conditions under which semiparametric efficiency bounds can be achieved in the presence of missing data due to dropout mechanisms We propose a comprehensive framework that builds on the principles of targeted maximum likelihood estimation TMLE and use of dynamic models to account for the dropout process explicitly Through a series of simulation studies we demonstrate the improved efficiency and robustness of our proposed methodology compared to traditional approaches which frequently rely on parametric assumptions or complete case analyses Additionally we apply our method to a realworld dataset on patient responses in a clinical trial illustrating its practical utility and the valuable insights it can provide in overcoming dropoutrelated biases Our findings establish a clear pathway for achieving semiparametric efficiency in longitudinal studies ultimately contributing to more reliable estimates and informed decisionmaking in research settings that routinely encounter dropout issues

author: Peter X. K. Song
text: In longitudinal data analysis with dropouts despite its local efficiency in theory the augmented inverse probability weighted AIPW estimator hardly achieves the semiparametric efficiency bound in practice even if the variancecovariance of the longitudinal outcomes is correctly modeled In this paper we propose a method based on conditional empirical likelihood Assuming missing at random MAR mechanism our estimator is doubly robust and locally efficient Unlike the AIPW estimator our estimator does not require to model any second moments including the variancecovariance of the longitudinal outcomes in order to achieve the semiparametric efficiency bound C Elsevier Inc

author: Peter X. K. Song
text: In longitudinal studies missing data is a prevalent issue that can significantly bias parameter estimates and compromise the validity of conclusions drawn from the analysis This paper investigates the validity of the ignorable missingness assumption in estimating equation approaches specifically tailored for longitudinal data We propose a novel framework that leverages both simulation studies and realworld datasets to evaluate the performance of various estimating equations under different missing data mechanisms The study systematically examines scenarios where the missingness is dependent on observed and unobserved data thereby challenging the ignorable missingness assumption Our findings highlight the implications of violating this assumption on the estimated parameters demonstrating that the bias and efficiency of estimators can vary widely based on the underlying missing data pattern Furthermore we introduce a set of practical diagnostic tools to aid researchers in assessing the validity of the ignorable missingness assumption in their analyses The results underscore the necessity of robust methodologies for handling missing data in longitudinal studies providing insights that could ultimately enhance the reliability and generalizability of longitudinal research outcomes

author: Peter X. K. Song
text: Quadratic inference functions QIF methodology is an important alternative to the generalized estimating equations GEE method in the longitudinal marginal model as it offers higher estimation efficiency than the GEE when correlation structure is misspecified The focus of this paper is on sample size determination and power calculation for QIF based on the Wald test in a marginal logistic model with covariates of treatment time and treatmenttime interaction We have made three contributions in this paper i we derived formulas of sample size and power for QIF and compared their performance with those given by the GEE ii we proposed an optimal scheme of sample size determination to overcome the difficulty of unknown true correlation matrix in the sense of minimal average risk and iii we studied properties of both QIF and GEE sample size formulas in relation to the number of followup visits and found that the QIF gave more robust sample sizes than the GEE Using numerical examples we illustrated that without sacrificing statistical power the QIF design leads to sample size saving and hence lower study cost in comparison with the GEE analysis We conclude that the QIF analysis is appealing for longitudinal studies Copyright c John Wiley Sons Ltd

author: Peter X. K. Song
text: This paper investigates the application of stationary state space models for analyzing longitudinal data offering a novel framework that enhances both estimation and inference in this context As longitudinal studies collect data over time from the same subjects traditional methods can suffer from issues related to autocorrelation and nonstationarity We propose a stationary state space model formulation that captures the underlying dynamics of longitudinal data while ensuring the process remains stationary over time We detail the models structure which incorporates both observed and latent variables and utilize advanced estimation techniques such as the Kalman filter to efficiently derive parameter estimates By applying our model to simulated data and realworld longitudinal datasets across various fields we demonstrate its robustness and flexibility in capturing temporal dependencies without running into nonstationary pitfalls Performance comparisons with existing methods highlight the advantages of our approach in terms of parameter estimation accuracy and predictive capability Ultimately this work contributes to the growing body of literature on time series analysis and provides a comprehensive toolset for researchers working with longitudinal data

author: Peter X. K. Song
text: This paper focuses on the problem of maximum likelihood estimation in linear mixedeffects models where outliers or unduly large observations are present in clustered or longitudinal data Multivariate t distributions are often imposed on either random effects andor random errors to incorporate outliers A powerful algorithm of maximum by parts MBP proposed by Song Fan and Kalbfleisch is implemented to obtain maximum likelihood estimators when the likelihood is intractable The computational efficiency of the MBP allows us to further apply a profilelikelihood technique for the estimation of the degrees of freedom in tdistributions Comparison of the Akaike information criterion AIC among candidate models provides an objective criterion to determine whether outliers are influential on the quality of model fit The proposed models and methods are illustrated through both simulation studies and data analysis examples with comparison to the existing EMalgorithm

author: Peter X. K. Song
text: The inverse probability weighted generalized estimating equations approach Robins et al Robins et al effectively removes bias and provides valid statistical inference for regression parameter estimation in marginal models when longitudinal data contain missing values The validity of the weighted generalized estimating equations regarding consistent estimation depends on whether the underlying missing data process is properly modelled However there is little work available to examine whether or not this condition holds In this paper we propose a test constructed from two sets of estimating equations one set is known to be unbiased but the other set is not known We utilize the quadratic inference function Qu et al method to assess their compatibility which is equivalent to testing for the validity of the weighted generalized estimating equations approach We conduct simulation studies to assess the performance of the proposed method The test procedure is illustrated through a real data example

author: Peter X. K. Song
text: The integration of multiple longitudinal studies presents unique challenges particularly when faced with studyspecific missing covariates that can bias estimates and hinder the robustness of conclusions This paper introduces a novel joint estimating function approach designed to effectively merge diverse datasets while simultaneously addressing the complications posed by nonrandomly missing covariates We employ a framework that incorporates information from all available studies allowing for flexible modeling of the longitudinal data structure alongside missingness patterns Our methodology leverages the strengths of generalized estimating equations GEEs and multiple imputation techniques to derive consistent estimates of model parameters and standard errors We validate our approach through extensive simulations that demonstrate improved performance over traditional methods in terms of bias reduction and efficiency Additionally we apply our framework to a realworld dataset comprising several health studies illustrating how our method enables comprehensive analyses and enhances the generalizability of findings across different populations Our results underscore the importance of properly addressing missing covariates in longitudinal studies setting the stage for future research in this critical area

author: Peter X. K. Song
text: The authors consider a class of state space models for the analysis of nonnormal longitudinal data whose latent process follows a stationary AR model with exponential dispersion model margins They propose to estimate parameters through an estimating equation approach based on the Kalman smoother This allows them to carry out a straightforward analysis of a wide range of nonnormal data They illustrate their approach via a simulation study and through analyses of Brazilian precipitation and US polio infection data

author: Peter X. K. Song
text: This paper presents a novel statistical framework for assessing model misspecification in stochastic diffusion models focusing on parametric structures commonly used in finance and economics We introduce the Information Ratio Test IRT a robust statistical test designed to evaluate the adequacy of parametric specifications by comparing modelimplied dynamics with observed data The IRT leverages the concept of information ratios providing a pragmatic measure of the tradeoff between model fit and complexity We derive theoretical properties of the IRT including asymptotic distributions and conditions for consistency and demonstrate its practical significance through simulation studies The proposed test is then applied to realworld financial time series showcasing its ability to detect subtle misspecifications that traditional goodnessoffit criteria may overlook Our findings highlight the IRT as a valuable tool for researchers and practitioners in refining stochastic models ultimately contributing to more accurate forecasting and risk management in uncertain environments

author: Peter X. K. Song
text: Merging multiple datasets collected from studies with identical or similar scientific objectives is often undertaken in practice to increase statistical power This article concerns the development of an effective statistical method that enables to merge multiple longitudinal datasets subject to various heterogeneous characteristics such as different followup schedules and studyspecific missing covariates eg covariates observed in some studies but missing in other studies The presence of studyspecific missing covariates presents great statistical methodology challenge in data merging and analysis We propose a joint estimating function approach to addressing this challenge in which a novel nonparametric estimating function constructed via splinesbased sieve approximation is utilized to bridge estimating equations from studies with missing covariates to those with fully observed covariates Under mild regularity conditions we show that the proposed estimator is consistent and asymptotically normal We evaluate finitesample performances of the proposed method through simulation studies In comparison to the conventional multiple imputation approach our method exhibits smaller estimation bias We provide an illustrative data analysis using longitudinal cohorts collected in Mexico City to assess the effect of lead exposures on childrens somatic growth

author: Peter X. K. Song
text: In this paper we introduce a novel state space model designed specifically for the analysis of multivariate longitudinal count data Longitudinal count data commonly encountered in fields such as epidemiology social sciences and ecology often exhibit complex temporal dynamics and correlations across multiple response variables Traditional analytical methods may fail to adequately capture these intricacies due to their limitations in flexibility and interpretability Our proposed state space framework addresses these challenges by leveraging hidden states that evolve over time allowing for both individuallevel variability and temporal correlation among count responses We employ a Bayesian approach for parameter estimation and model fitting enabling the incorporation of prior information and handling of missing data Through extensive simulation studies we evaluate the performance of our model in various scenarios demonstrating its robustness and efficiency Additionally we illustrate the applicability of our model using a realworld dataset revealing insightful patterns and dependencies in multivariate count outcomes over time Our findings contribute to the growing body of literature on longitudinal data analysis providing a powerful tool for researchers seeking to understand the joint dynamics of multivariate count processes

author: Peter X. K. Song
text: In various fields of research repeated measurements are often impacted by informative censoring where the likelihood of censoring is related to the underlying mechanisms driving the measurements This paper explores statistical methodologies tailored to analyze such datasets where traditional approaches may yield biased or inefficient estimates We propose a generalized linear mixed model that accounts for both the correlation of repeated measurements and the informative nature of censoring times Through extensive simulation studies we demonstrate the robustness of our method against various censoring scenarios comparing its performance to existing techniques We illustrate our findings with a realworld application in a longitudinal health study emphasizing the implications of our analysis for understanding the underlying processes Our results indicate that appropriately addressing informative censoring leads to more accurate parameter estimates and enhances the validity of conclusions drawn from repeated measurement data Finally we provide guidelines for practitioners to implement our approach in analyzing their datasets with informative censoring

author: Peter X. K. Song
text: In this paper we propose a novel approach for maximum likelihood inference in robust linear mixedeffects models by leveraging the flexibility of multivariate t distributions Traditional linear mixedeffects models often assume normality in the error structure which can lead to biased estimates and unreliable inference when faced with outliers or nonnormality in the data To address this limitation we introduce an augmented formulation of the linear mixedeffects model incorporating multivariate t distributions that allow for heavier tails and greater robustness against deviations from normality We derive the maximum likelihood estimates for the model parameters using a tailored ExpectationMaximization EM algorithm which facilitates convergence even in the presence of complex data structure Through simulation studies and realworld applications we demonstrate the efficacy of our proposed method in providing accurate parameter estimates improved robustness and valid inference compared to existing approaches Our findings highlight the advantages of utilizing multivariate t distributions in capturing the inherent variability of data thereby extending the applicability of mixedeffects modeling in fields such as psychology biology and social sciences where data irregularities are common

author: Peter X. K. Song
text: In the realm of statistical estimation and inference Quadratic Inference Functions QIFs offer a robust framework for analyzing complex data structures particularly in the presence of correlated observations However the efficiency of QIFs can be compromised by the presence of multicollinearity and model misspecifications This paper presents a novel approach to enhancing the performance of QIFs through the application of a linear shrinkage methodology By integrating linear shrinkage into the QIF framework we derive adjusted estimates that leverage both the advantages of QIFs and the regularization effects of shrinkage We systematically explore the theoretical foundations of this approach demonstrating its ability to improve estimation accuracy and reduce variance in highdimensional settings Through simulation studies and real data applications we illustrate the performance of the proposed linear shrinkage QIF against traditional QIF methods highlighting improvements in parameter estimation and inference accuracy The results suggest that our linear shrinkage technique not only mitigates common issues associated with QIFs but also provides a valuable tool for statisticians dealing with complex correlated data We conclude with practical recommendations for implementation and implications for future research

author: Peter X. K. Song
text: In the realm of biostatistical research particularly in longitudinal studies involving dichotomous outcomes determining an adequate sample size is crucial for ensuring the robustness and validity of statistical inference This paper presents a comprehensive framework for sample size determination when employing Quadratic Inference Functions QIF in longitudinal designs We explore the intricacies of QIF methodology in the context of binary responses addressing the challenges posed by correlation structures inherent in longitudinal data Using simulations and theoretical derivations we quantify the impact of parameters such as effect size expected correlation among repeated measures and variability of response rates on sample size calculations Our results highlight optimal sample sizes required for achieving desired power levels under different scenarios including variations in time points and treatment effects This study not only provides practical guidelines for researchers designing longitudinal studies but also enhances the understanding of the interplay between sample size data structure and inference accuracy in the application of QIFs The findings serve as a valuable resource for statisticians and researchers aiming to improve the design of studies with binary outcomes and ensure the reliability of their conclusions

author: Peter X. K. Song
text: In some commonly used longitudinal clinical trials designs the quadratic inference functions QIF method fails to work due to noninvertible estimation of the optimal weighting matrix We propose a modified QIF method in which the optimal weighting matrix is estimated by a linear shrinkage estimator replacing the sample covariance matrix We prove that the linear shrinkage estimator is consistent and asymptotically optimal under the expected quadratic loss and will have more stable numerical performance than the sample covariance matrix Simulations show that numerical improvements are acquired in light of a higher percentage of convergence and smaller standard errors and mean square errors of parameter estimates C Elsevier BV

author: Peter X. K. Song
text: AbstractThis paper evaluates the validity of Weighted Generalized Estimating Equations WGEE in analyzing correlated data structures commonly encountered in longitudinal and clusterbased studies Traditional Generalized Estimating Equations GEE offer a robust framework for estimating populationaveraged effects while accommodating withincluster correlation However the incorporation of weights can potentially enhance the efficiency and accuracy of these estimates especially in the presence of heterogeneous variances and missing data We conduct a comprehensive simulation study to assess the performance of WGEE compared to its unweighted counterpart focusing on parameter estimation standard error estimation and coverage probabilities The simulations explore various data generating mechanisms including different correlation structures and weighting schemes Additionally we apply WGEE to realworld datasets to illustrate its practical applicability and interpretability in empirical research Our findings indicate that WGEE can provide marked improvements in estimation under certain conditions although the effectiveness is heavily influenced by the appropriateness of the chosen weights We conclude by discussing the implications of our results for applied statisticians and researchers emphasizing the importance of considering model assumptions and weighting strategies when employing WGEE in practice

author: Peter X. K. Song
text: We develop a hypothesis testing approach to checking model misspecification on parametric structures in continuoustime stochastic diffusion models The key idea behind the development of our test statistic is rooted in a ratio of two types of information matrices the negative sensitivity matrix and the variability matrix in the context of martingale estimating equations We propose a bootstrap resampling method to implement numerically the proposed diagnostic procedure Through intensive simulation studies we compare the proposed approach with several currently popular methods and show that our approach is advantageous in the aspects of type I error control power improvement as well as computational efficiency Two realworld data examples are included to illustrate the practical use of our proposed testing procedure C Elsevier BV

author: Peter X. K. Song
text: Incomplete repeated measurement data often arise in medical studies A problem that has recently drawn much attention in the literature in this situation is that the incompleteness or missingness is informative or related to the underlying variable of interest In this paper we propose a nonparametric global test for treatment comparison in the presence of informative incompleteness A semiparametric regression model is also presented for assessing conditional treatment effects given the dropout patterns adopting the idea similar to that behind the patternmixture modelling approach and discussed in Shih and Quan The proposed methods can be easily implemented and are conceptually simple and similar too but can be applied to more general cases than those given in Yao et al They are evaluated by numerical studies and applied to data from a clinical trial of adult schizophrenics Copyright C John Wiley Sons Ltd

author: Peter X. K. Song
text: We propose a nonstationary state space model for multivariate longitudinal count data driven by a latent gamma Markov process The Poisson counts are assumed to be conditionally independent given the latent process both over time and across categories We consider a regression model where timevarying covariates may enter via either the Poisson model or the latent gamma process Estimation is based on the Kalman smoother and we consider analysis of residuals from both the Poisson model and the latent process A reanalysis of Zegers polio data shows that the choice between a stationary and nonstationary model is crucial for the correct assessment of the evidence of a longterm decrease in the rate of US polio infection
